common_name: Osiris Fantaisie Ligularia (Compact Bicolor Purple-Backed Foliage)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in constantly moist, humus-rich soil in partial shade with protection from afternoon sun; Osiris Fantaisie is a compact Quebec-bred ligularia cultivar, more manageable in a smaller bed than full-sized types like Desdemona, but like all ligularias it needs a cool, sheltered, consistently damp site to perform well in zone 9 heat.

directions: Plant in constantly moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic soil in partial shade with protection from afternoon sun and heat; Osiris Fantaisie is a compact ligularia cultivar bred at Les Jardins Osiris in Quebec, bearing leathery, heart-shaped leaves in deep olive-green flushed burgundy on top with contrasting purple undersides and purple stems, topped in summer by racemes of bright yellow daisy flowers. Its more compact size, to about three feet, makes it easier to fit into a smaller shade bed than larger ligularia cultivars. Like all ligularias it wilts visibly during midday heat and recovers overnight, normal behavior for the genus that signals a need for cooler, damper conditions rather than disease; give it the coolest, most sheltered, consistently moist spot available and mulch heavily to protect the roots through a Gulf South summer. Divide congested clumps in early spring every few years to maintain vigor.

common_name: Miyazaki Toad Lily (Award-Winning Densely Flowered Cultivar)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Miyazaki was rated the top performer for floral display among 24 toad lily types evaluated in the Chicago Botanic Garden's 2001 plant trial.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to deep shade; Miyazaki is an outstanding toad lily selection that consistently rated as the best floral performer among two dozen cultivars trialed at the Chicago Botanic Garden, thanks to arching stems densely packed with white, purple-freckled, orchid-like flowers along nearly the entire stem length rather than clustered only at the tips. It blooms in late summer into fall, exactly when the shade garden most needs fresh color, and the glossy, clasping leaves stay attractive through the growing season. It spreads gradually to form an expanding colony in a consistently moist, shaded woodland setting. Keep soil evenly moist and mulch with leaf litter, and divide congested clumps in spring if flowering begins to decline.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden — Tricyrtis Plant Evaluation
North Carolina State Extension — Plant Toolbox

common_name: Gilty Pleasure Toad Lily (Gold-Foliage Fall-Blooming Cultivar)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Gilty Pleasure is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction grown as much for its gold foliage as its flowers, giving season-long color in a shade bed rather than only at bloom time.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to deep shade; Gilty Pleasure stands apart from most toad lily cultivars for its gold foliage, which holds bright color through the growing season rather than staying plain green, providing a long season of interest well before the lavender-pink, deeply freckled, orchid-like flowers open in fall. The gold leaf color develops best with some morning light but stays attractive even in fairly deep shade. As with other Formosa toad lilies, it is more heat tolerant than the Japanese species, making it a good choice for zone 7-9 shade gardens. Keep soil evenly moist and mulch with leaf litter, and divide congested clumps in spring as needed to maintain vigor.

common_name: Blue Wonder Toad Lily (Compact Heavy Shade-Tolerant Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to deep shade; Blue Wonder is a compact toad lily hybrid noted for good tolerance of heavy shade, useful for the darkest corners of a woodland bed where many flowering perennials fail.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to deep shade; Blue Wonder is a compact toad lily hybrid bearing creamy white to powder-blue flowers heavily speckled with blue-purple spots, blooming from September into frost when most of the shade garden has finished flowering for the season. Its notably good tolerance of heavy shade makes it a useful choice for the darker, more enclosed corners of a woodland garden where many flowering shade perennials struggle to bloom well. The compact, upright habit fits neatly into a mixed shade border without sprawling. Keep soil evenly moist and mulch with leaf litter, and divide congested clumps in spring if flowering begins to decline.

common_name: Lightning Strike Toad Lily (Variegated Gold-and-Green Foliage Cultivar)

planting.note: Plant divisions in fall or early spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to mostly shade with even moisture; Lightning Strike is a Japanese selection valued for boldly striped gold-and-green variegated foliage in addition to its typical toad lily flowers.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to mostly shade with consistent moisture; Lightning Strike is a striking variegated toad lily, its arching stems and leaves streaked in gold and green like bolts of lightning, providing strong foliage interest for months before the mauve-purple, heavily spotted flowers open on two-foot arching stems in late summer to fall. Because the variegation develops best with a bit more light than deep shade allows, give it a spot with morning sun or dappled light rather than the darkest part of the garden. Keep soil evenly moist and mulch with leaf litter, and divide congested clumps in spring as needed to maintain the plant's vigor and variegation quality.
